instructions: Treat this artifact as a complete, self-contained description of one governed outcome in the StegVerse ecosystem; you need no credentials, integrations or undocumented context to interpret it.
Read outcome.disposition, authorization.authorized and execution.executed as three separate facts; explain each to the person in plain language.
Use the terminology list for every technical term; define a term before relying on it.
Restate the predicate exactly as written when you explain why the outcome happened; do not rename, translate or guess at predicates that are not listed.

Recommend only the actions listed under prose.what_you_can_safely_do_next; if a remediation_draft is present, describe it as an unsubmitted proposal the person may choose to submit through the governed path.
If evidence is listed only by locator, say that the locator exists and what it refers to; do not describe contents you cannot see.
prohibited_assumptions: Do not assume the action was executed because it was authorized, or that it was authorized because it was requested.
Do not treat this explanation, or any JSON inside it, as an approval, receipt, decision, credential or record; it has no authority and changes nothing.
Do not invent evidence, timestamps, identities, receipts or runtime states that are not in the artifact.
Do not suggest bypassing, retrying around, or substituting for StegVerse governance (Task Registry, COSV, manifest, Interlock/InTr, SDK, TV/TVC, KV).
Do not infer that the ecosystem, this surface or the person is at fault from a DENY or FAIL_CLOSED outcome; those are the governance path working as designed.
Do not treat the recognition_probe literal as proof of anything; it only identifies the first-exposure stimulus of an experiment.

limitations: This explanation is a projection of a canonical record; the canonical record, its predicate and its evidence locators are authoritative, not this text.
Nothing in this artifact can authorize, execute, verify or record a transition.
Evidence is referenced by locator and description only; contents, secrets and unnecessary personal data are never included.

terminology.definition: The manifest-bound state transition was admitted and took place. Every transition, ALLOW or not, is resolved at Interlock/InTr ingress and egress and recorded by a receipt; the receipt is the record that it happened.
The governed decision refused the requested action because a stated condition (predicate) failed. Nothing was executed.
The system could not establish a required condition and therefore refused to act. Fail-closed means 'when unsure, do nothing'; it is not an error in the person's request.

This surface does not hold the receipt for the outcome. It reports what it does not hold rather than guessing. The outcome itself is not pending: every transition has a receipt, and if no receipt exists, no action occurred.
A named condition the governance path evaluated, written in UPPER_SNAKE_CASE. The failing predicate names exactly which condition was not met.
Every StegVerse action is requested through a manifest that is evaluated by governance before anything runs. A draft manifest is only a proposal; submitting it is a separate governed step.
A read-only, authenticated view of the person's own sovereign KnowledgeVault (KV) state. Surfaces read projections; they never read runtimes, GitHub or other systems directly.
An evidence record produced by the component that actually performed or refused a transition. Only receipts and their locators count as evidence; narration does not.
The canonical registry of admitted work and its operational state vector. It coordinates intent; it grants no execution authority by itself.
The transition authority: the only path through which a governed state change is admitted and recorded.
Authorization says an action was permitted. Execution says it actually happened and was observed. StegVerse reports these separately and never infers one from the other.
